newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma-Canada copper mine to start output in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Burma-Canada copper mine to start output in 1998.

text.p: A Burmese-Canadian joint venture is scheduled to start producing about 25,000 tonnes of copper annually from a mine in north western Burma in 1998, official media said on Tuesday.

State-run newspapers quoted Jack Devitt, vice chairman of Myanmar Ivanhoe Copper Joint Venture Co, as saying preparatory works had been undertaken for the project to start production at its Letpadaung Hill mine, about 600 miles northwest of Rangoon.
He said the mine was estimated to hold more than 400 million tonnes of copper reserves.
Devitt said the company's expected 25,000-tonne initial annual output was projected to rise to 63,000 tonnes by mid-2000.
Vancouver-based Ivanhoe Capital Corp entered the joint venture with the Ministry of Mines in April 1996.
